The core REST module is `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`. Its `omod` (web) layer calls `EncounterService.saveEncounter` directly in three places, all for the `encounter` and `encounterprovider` resources. The `api` module has no calls. The 1.9 `EncounterResource` overrides `save`, so its `1_8` counterpart only runs for the 1.8 resource version. Each of these callers is reached through the generic CRUD `save`/`delete` path, so a behaviour change in `saveEncounter` would show up in `POST`/`POST {uuid}` on `/ws/rest/v1/encounter` and `/ws/rest/v1/encounterprovider`, and in `DELETE` on `encounterprovider`.

**Production callers (best first):**
1. `EncounterResource1_9.save` (`openmrs1_9`) overrides `save`, sets the provider back-references, then calls `saveEncounter`. This is the live path for `/ws/rest/v1/encounter` on OpenMRS 1.9–2.1.
2. `EncounterResource1_8.save` (`openmrs1_8`) is the base `save` that `EncounterResource1_9` overrides. It is the live path for 1.8.
3. `EncounterProviderResource1_9.save` adds the provider to the encounter, then calls `saveEncounter` on the parent encounter (line 186) and returns the matching `EncounterProvider`.
4. `EncounterProviderResource1_9.delete` voids the matching provider, then calls `saveEncounter` on the parent encounter (line 174).

**Test callers (would need updating if the contract changed):**
- `omod/src/test/.../openmrs1_9/EncounterController1_9Test.java` lines 532 and 553.
- `omod/src/test/.../openmrs1_10/OrderController1_10Test.java` line 355.

Falkon searches covered all 42 repositories with no `limit` truncation for this repo, but I did not check for indirect callers that reach `saveEncounter` through other service methods.
